fatal_errors: The specific AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy and its as-cast FCC+B2 microstructure are not identified.
The hypothesis conflates thermal aging treatments with tensile testing at different temperatures.
It omits the approximately 550-750°C aging window and the critical 600°C embrittlement and 750°C recovery conditions.
It incorrectly predicts recovery upon returning to lower temperature rather than recovery after higher-temperature aging.
The proposed generic phase-transformation mechanism misses enhanced L12 ordering, elevated APBE, planar slip, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, and boundary-tip stress concentration.
No evidence is cited, and the proposed experiment cannot distinguish the target mechanism from generic temperature-dependent ductility changes.
explanation: The generated hypothesis only restates a generic temperature-dependent loss of ductility in unspecified high-entropy alloys. It neither identifies the target eutectic HEA nor reconstructs the non-monotonic aging response. Although it broadly anticipates ductility loss and subsequent recovery, the recovery direction and experimental framing are inconsistent with the target. Its mechanism, baseline, boundaries, and falsification test are too nonspecific to establish the ordering- and phase-boundary-mediated ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
